overview.reason: NWFM enforces one tenant per deployment and database; the controls below cover identity, data, queues, cache, files and operations. Shared-database hosting is unsupported and rejected.

identity.reason: Signed sessions bind the configured tenant, persisted session and current security stamp. Current user/team/permission state is checked server-side; request selectors cannot replace that scope.

database.reason: SQL Server databases are durably assigned to one tenant before migrations. Normal connections cannot administer the database or rewrite ownership. EF workflow filters and immutable tenant writes add defense in depth; discovery covers every mapped entity.

cache.reason: All cache operations use server environment and tenant namespaces; resource keys retain user/result inputs and expiry. Permission validation reads current grants. There are no intentionally shared protected entries.

resources.reason: Dedicated tenant processes/workers use bounded HTTP/principal/IP/login rates, concurrent requests, SQL pools and transactional pending-queue capacities. Aggregate infrastructure CPU/memory/I/O limits must also be deployed.

credentials.reason: Service keys require tenant, environment, permission scope and a constant-time hashed-key match. Webhooks bind the canonical tenant/connection/method/path/body/timestamp context. Passwords use ASP.NET Identity hashing.

async.reason: Each worker belongs to one bound database and verifies active tenant admission. Tenant-owned queue records, authenticated ingress, scoped idempotency, retry and capacity controls preserve the producer/consumer boundary.

storage.reason: Each storage root has a durable tenant marker. Exact file access is mediated by the tenant database/API; canonical relative paths, link rejection, size limits and collision refusal prevent escaping or poisoning the root.

lifecycle.reason: Bootstrap binds isolated resources; active-state admission and session revocation stop offboarded access. The offline operator workflow and proposed retention policy require deployment execution and evidence across backups, exports, replicas and legal holds.

audit.reason: Request/security events carry server tenant context and trace IDs without OTPs, tokens or message bodies. Audit reads use the bound database and existing permissions; the production collector, alert routing and immutable retention store require deployment verification.

boundaries.reason: The dedicated database and immutable row ownership, environment/tenant cache namespaces, and durably bound file root each preserve the server-owned tenant context. The grouped positive and negative tests exercise all three boundaries.

rate-review.reason: Configurable per-process windows, principal/IP limits, concurrency and transactional queue admission exist; aggregate gateway counters and capacity sizing remain deployment work.

storage-review.reason: Exact tenant-local file IDs, operation policies, uploader/pending/submitted state, pinned upload schemas and canonical storage paths are enforced; no signed URL or object-version API exists.

lifecycle-review.reason: Transactional ownership binding/offboarding and isolated restore verification exist; full resource provisioning, destructive retention, external credential rotation and protected operational audit delivery are deployment responsibilities.

credential-issuance-review.reason: The optional inbound service-key verifier stores only a SHA-256 digest with tenant/environment/scopes. Credential issuance is an operator responsibility; passwords retain Identity password hashing.

audit-review.reason: Verified tenant/nullable actor/trace denial events and restricted lifecycle audit writes exist. Collector authorization, durable append-only protection for all required audit classes, tamper detection, alert delivery and retention require deployment evidence.

controls.heading: Introduction
controls.requirement: Multi-tenant applications serve multiple customers (tenants) from a shared infrastructure, codebase, and often shared databases. This architecture is the foundation of modern SaaS platforms, offering cost efficiency and simplified operations.

controls.heading: Introduction

controls.heading: Scope Tenant Context to the Transaction
controls.requirement: A normal `SET` persists until the session ends after its transaction commits, while [`SET LOCAL` lasts only for the current transaction](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set.html). When an application or connection pool reuses a database session without resetting it, session-scoped tenant state can therefore be inherited by the next request.

controls.requirement: - When tenants share capacity or quotas, include tenant identity as one rate-limit dimension alongside any required global, endpoint, user, or IP limits.

controls.heading: API Security & Rate Limiting
controls.requirement: - Rate limits at the HTTP boundary do not constrain every shared resource. Where tenant load can affect other tenants, apply tenant-aware limits or scheduling to the relevant bottlenecks, such as concurrent work, queued messages, database connections, fan-out, CPU, or memory. Retain global safety limits, and isolate a worker or resource pool when the risk or service commitment justifies the operational cost. The [AWS SaaS Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/saas-lens/pe-selection.html) describes scaling, throttling, and selective resource isolation as complementary noisy-neighbor controls.
controls.reason: Dedicated tenant processes/workers use bounded HTTP/principal/IP/login rates, concurrent requests, SQL pools and transactional pending-queue capacities. Aggregate infrastructure CPU/memory/I/O limits must also be deployed.

controls.heading: API Security & Rate Limiting
controls.requirement: - Choose tenant quotas and limits according to capacity, abuse risk, contractual quotas, and service tiers rather than arbitrary hardcoded values. Support appropriate time windows and burst controls where applicable.
controls.reason: Request, principal/IP, login, concurrency, SQL-pool and queue limits are configurable and validated. Fixed one-minute windows and immediate concurrency rejection exist; defaults are engineering bounds, not a contractual capacity assessment.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Size and approve budgets from load/abuse tests and tenant commitments. Configure burst protection at the gateway where fixed windows are insufficient; retain host-wide limits.

controls.heading: API Security & Rate Limiting
controls.requirement: - Use shared counters with atomic updates when limits must apply across multiple application instances.
controls.reason: Request counters are process-local; the application does not implement shared atomic HTTP rate counters. SQL queue admission is atomic across writers but is not a distributed HTTP limiter. The supported dedicated deployment still needs an aggregate budget if replicated.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Before using replicas with a shared tenant quota, deploy and test atomic shared gateway counters (including burst/window behavior), or keep that workload single-process. Test simultaneous replicas; do not multiply a contractual allowance by replica count.

controls.heading: API Security & Rate Limiting
controls.requirement: - Communicate throttling appropriately, such as returning HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header where applicable.
controls.reason: Request/principal/concurrency rejection returns HTTP 429 and Retry-After; the exception handler also maps queue saturation to 429 with Retry-After 60. Denial telemetry records the final response after exception handling.

controls.heading: API Security & Rate Limiting
controls.requirement: - Validate server-verified tenant context on every tenant-scoped API request, and mount tenant-aware middleware only on routes where tenant context is required. Public or global endpoints need no artificial tenant context.
controls.reason: Current signed sessions are bound to the server tenant and current membership; selectors cannot replace it. Tenant checks apply to API paths; non-API paths bypass the budget middleware and public sign-in metadata does not require a fabricated authenticated actor.

controls.heading: API Security & Rate Limiting
controls.requirement: - Bind API credentials to explicit tenant sets, environments, and permission scopes. An intentionally cross-tenant service identity must be separately authorized and least privileged.
controls.reason: Service keys require tenant, environment, permission scope and a constant-time hashed-key match. Webhooks bind the canonical tenant/connection/method/path/body/timestamp context. Passwords use ASP.NET Identity hashing.

controls.heading: API Security & Rate Limiting
controls.requirement: - When B2B request signing is required, bind the signature to the security-relevant request context, such as tenant selection, target audience, method, path, body digest, and expiration, as applicable.
controls.reason: Service keys require tenant, environment, permission scope and a constant-time hashed-key match. Webhooks bind the canonical tenant/connection/method/path/body/timestamp context. Passwords use ASP.NET Identity hashing.

controls.reason: Each worker belongs to one bound database and verifies active tenant admission. Tenant-owned queue records, authenticated ingress, scoped idempotency, retry and capacity controls preserve the producer/consumer boundary.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Classify stored objects as global, tenant-scoped, or user-scoped. Keep intentionally shared assets in an explicit global namespace.
controls.reason: Each storage root has a durable tenant marker. Exact file access is mediated by the tenant database/API; canonical relative paths, link rejection, size limits and collision refusal prevent escaping or poisoning the root.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Partition tenant-scoped objects with a tenant-aware object key, bucket, account, or enforceable storage policy. Object naming or prefixes alone are not authorization boundaries.
controls.reason: Tenant files use a dedicated durably bound local root and tenant database lookups; identifiers and prefixes are not authorization. Operation handlers enforce file permissions before storage access, with path and link defenses.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Enforce separate OS identities/ACLs and volumes for tenant services; prove another deployment cannot directly read the root or its backups. The marker alone is not an OS boundary.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Validate tenant identifiers against an allowlisted canonical format, alongside object-path validation. Reject absolute paths, `..` traversal components, and path-separator tricks that could escape the tenant namespace.
controls.reason: Storage accepts a nonempty server-configured Guid tenant and verifies the durable marker. Relative-path validation rejects rooted paths, traversal, empty components, reserved markers, alternate streams and redirected ancestors; upload names are generated file IDs.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Authorize the exact tenant, object, and operation before you upload or download an object, delete it, or generate a signed URL.
controls.reason: Upload commands require FormUploaders and resolve the exact form/schema version before writing. Read/delete look up an active tenant-local file ID and enforce FormFileAccess; delete additionally requires pending state and never removes migrated archive bytes. There is no signed URL or arbitrary object-version API.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Verify object ownership where appropriate; do not trust client-supplied tenant metadata as authorization proof.
controls.reason: The dedicated database/root binding determines tenant ownership. Pending-file access uses the server-recorded uploader; submitted reads use current review/task permission and delete uses owner/admin plus pending state. Client path/context/tenant metadata is not accepted as storage ownership proof.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Restrict signed URLs to the required object and operation, with an appropriate expiration and revocation model. The tenant identifier does not need to appear in the URL when authorization happened before signing.
controls.reason: NWFM does not issue signed object URLs. Downloads resolve tenant-local file IDs and current operation authorization. A future signed-URL feature must bind the exact object/version and operation, expiry and revocation and add negative tests before use.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Ensure tenant deletion targets only that tenant's objects. Use an exact tenant-prefix boundary, such as `tenants/acme/` rather than `tenants/acme`, because the latter could also match `tenants/acme-west/`.
controls.reason: Local DeleteAsync enforces the exact canonical path below the bound root, and API deletion checks the individual pending file. There is no bulk tenant-prefix deletion API; offboarding records a schedule rather than recursively deleting resources.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Retention operators must verify the exact owned volume/database/cache namespace and delimiter boundary before deletion, including sibling-prefix negative tests. Do not generalize a tenant label into a prefix search.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Account for object versions, replicas, and backups when applying retention and deletion policies.
controls.reason: Retention schedules and legal holds are recorded by operator tooling. Local files have immutable IDs/no-overwrite behavior, but the application does not enumerate or purge storage-provider versions, replicas, exports or backups.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Inventory every retained copy and execute/verify expiry or deletion per store, including versions and replicas. Legal holds block deletion and restrict access; preserve evidence from the actual storage/backup service.

controls.heading: 6. File Storage & Blob Isolation
controls.requirement: - Use tenant-specific encryption keys when required by the risk or compliance model; shared managed keys with enforced access context may also be appropriate.
controls.reason: Dedicated database/root/identity boundaries and documented encryption policy exist; the repository does not provision cloud KMS or prove encryption-at-rest or tenant-specific key custody.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Configure managed encryption with isolated access context, dedicated keys where risk/contract requires, and prove rotation/recovery. Keep key destruction gated on all retained copies and legal holds.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security
controls.requirement: - Implement secure tenant provisioning with isolated resources. Treat onboarding as an all-or-nothing operation: if a step fails, remove partially created resources and record the failure.
controls.reason: Database ownership binding and its Provisioned ledger insert are transactional; the request host refuses administrator identity and startup mutation. That ledger event is not proof that later module migrations/seeds or external resource allocation all completed. No full infrastructure provisioning orchestrator exists.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Provision into quarantine without traffic; activate only after all resources/migrations/checks succeed. On failure record the partial attempt externally and clean only resources owned by that attempt, preserving existing tenant data. Test failure at each stage.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security
controls.requirement: - Generate unique encryption keys per tenant where required.
controls.reason: Bootstrap binds isolated resources; active-state admission and session revocation stop offboarded access. The offline operator workflow and proposed retention policy require deployment execution and evidence across backups, exports, replicas and legal holds.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Execute and retain the applicable deployment evidence in docs/security/tenant-security.md. CI does not attest production isolation, key custody, retention, restore drills or alert delivery.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security
controls.requirement: - Generate tenant API credentials with a cryptographically secure random generator and at least 128 bits of entropy. Return each credential once and store only a hash, never the plaintext value. An approved hash function such as SHA-256 is enough for a high-entropy random key, as [NIST SP 800-63B](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#lookupver) allows for look-up secrets. It does not protect low-entropy or user-chosen secrets; store those according to the [Password Storage Cheat Sheet](Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.md).
controls.reason: The optional inbound service-key verifier compares a SHA-256 digest in constant time and binds tenant/environment/scopes; password storage uses Identity hashing. There is no public tenant API-key issuance endpoint and the verifier cannot establish entropy from a digest.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Issue inbound API keys with a CSPRNG (at least 128 bits; use 32 random bytes), deliver once through an authenticated secret channel, retain only ApiKeySha256 in verifier configuration, and disable/revoke old keys. Never use a fast digest for user-chosen passwords or log plaintext issuance.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security
controls.requirement: - Apply a documented retention and deletion policy to every place tenant data lives: active stores, caches, object versions, replicas, exports, backups, and encryption keys. Restrict access to records kept for legal reasons.
controls.reason: The operator records active-data/backup/audit deadlines and legal hold. Policy covers all stores and encryption keys; the application does not automate destructive retention or claim that a schedule constitutes deletion.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Maintain a copy/key inventory for active stores, caches, versions, replicas, exports, backups and holds. Execute approved deletion/expiry and restrict retained records; retain evidence and recovery dependencies.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security
controls.requirement: - During offboarding, put the tenant into a state that rejects new operations, then revoke all active sessions, API keys, and other tenant-scoped credentials.
controls.reason: OffboardAsync atomically makes the database inactive, revokes refresh/SSO sessions, changes stamps, locks accounts and records the operator. API and delayed workers recheck active state. External service/webhook credentials are rejected by inactive admission but are not erased or rotated by that transaction.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Drain already authorized in-flight effects, revoke/disable all externally configured service, webhook and signing credentials, and rotate before any reactivation. Capture denial tests for API and workers as well as provider revocation evidence.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security
controls.requirement: - When the retention policy permits deletion, remove the tenant's active data, cached data, and stored objects. Delete a tenant encryption key only after every copy encrypted under it, including backups, replicas, and records under legal hold, has passed its retention period, unless you intend to destroy those copies too.
controls.reason: Retention policy delays active-data/backup expiry and respects legal holds; operator tooling never automatically destroys production stores or keys. Current code does not assert that scheduled dates prove removal.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Delete only after the approved deadline/holds permit it. Delete or expire all encrypted copies before destroying their key unless deliberate cryptographic destruction is approved; record the effect on backups, replicas and held records.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security
controls.requirement: - Maintain an audit trail of provisioning and deprovisioning, including failed and partial operations.
controls.reason: Boundary provisioning and successful offboarding record SQL ORIGINAL_LOGIN in LifecycleAudit; authorized restore verification records success or denial. Full provisioning failures and rolled-back offboarding attempts are not durably recorded by those same successful transactions.
controls.deploymentRequirement: The operator/provisioner must record failed and partial attempts in a separately protected sink, with verified target/actor/reason/outcome and no secrets. Do not count the initial Provisioned binding event as full provisioning success.

controls.heading: 7. Tenant Onboarding & Offboarding Security

controls.reason: Bootstrap binds isolated resources; active-state admission and session revocation stop offboarded access. The offline operator workflow and proposed retention policy require deployment execution and evidence across backups, exports, replicas and legal holds.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Include server-verified tenant context in tenant-scoped security and audit events, and record the authenticated actor (user or service identity) when available. Do not require an authenticated actor for events where none exists; global infrastructure events may have no tenant.
controls.reason: Denial events include server tenant, final status, trace and a nullable actor Guid only from an authenticated, unambiguous tenant-bound principal. Anonymous/early denials have no actor. Lifecycle operations record SQL ORIGINAL_LOGIN; global/aggregate events do not invent an individual actor.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Preserve these structured fields in collection; classify all audit producers and service identities. Verify downstream storage/indexing and avoid substituting user headers for actor identity.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - A centralized audit store is acceptable when read access enforces tenant scope. Cross-tenant audit reads and writes require explicit platform authorization.
controls.reason: Application audit reads remain inside the dedicated tenant database and existing permission boundary. Lifecycle administration uses a separate SQL operator identity; no centralized multi-tenant audit API is implemented.
controls.deploymentRequirement: If centralizing logs, enforce tenant-scoped reader views and separate least-privileged platform read/write roles. Test both reads and ingestion authorization with two tenant identities.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Distinguish tenant audit readers from platform auditors. Tenant administrator rights must not grant platform-wide audit access.
controls.reason: A tenant Administrator is confined to its deployment and does not become the offline SQL tenant operator or a platform collector administrator. The application has no platform-wide audit browsing endpoint.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Provision separate collector/platform auditor roles; never map the tenant Administrator claim to cross-tenant audit access. Test denial using actual deployed identities.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Enforce append-only audit behavior through database permissions or storage controls such as write-once, read-many (WORM) rather than relying on application-level methods alone.
controls.reason: Startup refuses a request identity that can mutate Tenancy.LifecycleAudit; documented operator grants allow INSERT without UPDATE/DELETE. Ordinary Workflow audit rows under schema CRUD are not a WORM ledger, and application append-only methods alone do not protect them from SQL writers.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Enforce and test append-only/WORM retention for every required audit class, including durable collection of Workflow audit records; deny update/delete to writers/readers or use an independently protected collector. Lifecycle role checks alone are insufficient for all audit data.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Use tamper-evident mechanisms to detect modifications to stored audit records; tamper detection identifies modifications rather than preventing them.
controls.reason: The repository emits structured events and protects ordinary lifecycle writes but implements no cryptographic audit chain, signed checkpoint or storage-integrity verifier. Append-only permissions are prevention and must not be described as tamper detection.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Select a tamper-evident audit facility, protect verification keys/checkpoints separately, and demonstrate detection of altered/deleted records. Retain verification evidence independently of the application database.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Monitor denied or unexpected cross-tenant access attempts without treating explicitly authorized platform operations as violations.
controls.reason: Request/security events carry server tenant context and trace IDs without OTPs, tokens or message bodies. Audit reads use the bound database and existing permissions; the production collector, alert routing and immutable retention store require deployment verification.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Execute and retain the applicable deployment evidence in docs/security/tenant-security.md. CI does not attest production isolation, key custody, retention, restore drills or alert delivery.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Alert on tenant-isolation control failures and repeated suspicious denial patterns.
controls.reason: TenantSecuritySignals emits denial event 4201 and bounded repeated-denial alert 4202 (20 in 60 seconds, at most once/minute). Startup fails on isolation violations; neither emission nor refusal proves alert delivery.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Route repeated-denial and startup-boundary failures to the protected collector/on-call destination. Test notification delivery and documented response; distinguish authorized platform operations.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Explicitly exclude secrets from logs and minimize sensitive tenant data. Mask or otherwise protect sensitive fields that genuinely need to be retained, according to the applicable policy.
controls.reason: Denial events use bounded identifiers/status/trace rather than request credentials or exception bodies. SMS logging omits recipient/OTP/message contents. Lifecycle reason/backup references are operator-supplied metadata and must not contain secrets; this is not a claim that every business audit payload is nonsensitive.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Classify and minimize each audit payload; restrict/mask retained PII and prevent collector access to tokens, credentials and raw request bodies. Review new producers and exception logging for sensitive content.

controls.heading: 8. Logging, Monitoring & Audit
controls.requirement: - Apply the documented access and retention policy for each audit-data class.
controls.reason: Request/security events carry server tenant context and trace IDs without OTPs, tokens or message bodies. Audit reads use the bound database and existing permissions; the production collector, alert routing and immutable retention store require deployment verification.
controls.deploymentRequirement: Execute and retain the applicable deployment evidence in docs/security/tenant-security.md. CI does not attest production isolation, key custody, retention, restore drills or alert delivery.

controls.requirement: - Configure collection, protection, and retention according to the [OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html).
controls.reason: The repository provides structured tenant security signals, lifecycle records and policy documentation. It does not configure production collection, WORM storage, alert destinations, key custody or per-class retention.

controls.heading: Do's and Don'ts / Don't
controls.requirement: - Treat tenant IDs from client headers or request parameters as authorization proof; they are selectors that require server-side verification.
controls.reason: Signed sessions bind the configured tenant, persisted session and current security stamp. Current user/team/permission state is checked server-side; request selectors cannot replace that scope.

controls.heading: Do's and Don'ts / Don't
